question: Which of the following describes the function of the Memory Address Register (MAR) in a CPU?
options: Stores the actual data being transferred to and from memory
Holds the memory address location from which data will be fetched or where data will be stored
Performs arithmetic logic addition and division
Contains the next program instruction awaiting decoding
explanation: MAR (Memory Address Register) holds the memory address of the data or instruction that needs to be accessed by the CPU[cite: 1].

question: In the context of the CPU data processing cycle, what is the role of the Memory Buffer Register (MBR) / Memory Data Register (MDR)?
options: Acts as a permanent database engine
Contains the data to be written into or read from the addressed memory location
Translates high-level source code into binary format
Controls the physical rotation speed of secondary storage drives
explanation: The Memory Buffer Register (MBR) or Memory Data Register (MDR) holds the contents of memory read from or to be written to memory[cite: 5].

question: What type of primary memory uses Content Addressable Memory (CAM) principles to search data by content rather than by address?
explanation: In Information Technology, Associative Memory is also known as Content Addressable Memory (CAM) because items are accessed based on their data contents rather than addresses[cite: 1].

question: Which of the following represents a major operational disadvantage of Dynamic RAM (DRAM)?
options: It requires periodic refreshing thousands of times per second because capacitors lose their charge
It is an optical medium that is impossible to rewrite
It is slower than magnetic tape drives
explanation: DRAM uses capacitors that leak charge and thus requires continuous, periodic electrical refresh cycles[cite: 1, 5].

question: What is the typical time limit before a dynamic RAM (DRAM) memory cell must undergo a refresh cycle?
explanation: DRAM cells must typically be refreshed every few milliseconds (commonly within 2 ms to 4 ms) to retain stored binary bits[cite: 5].

question: What type of ROM is pre-programmed with permanent data during the fabrication process at the factory and cannot be altered afterward?
explanation: Mask ROM (MROM) chips are hardwired with fixed data during manufacturing and cannot be reprogrammed or modified[cite: 5].

question: Which software protocol or hardware routine is executed immediately to prepare the computer for operation when the power switch is turned on?
explanation: The Bootstrap Loader is an initial program stored in ROM that loads the operating system into main memory during system startup[cite: 5].

question: In a CPU, what is the collection of interconnected flip-flops acting as a single storage unit called?
explanation: A Register is an internal high-speed CPU memory circuit made up of a group of flip-flops capable of storing multi-bit binary words[cite: 5].

question: Which of the following is considered a Sequential Access storage medium?
explanation: Magnetic Tape is a sequential access medium because data must be read or written in linear order from beginning to end[cite: 1, 5].

question: What does the abbreviation DASD stand for in IBM and IT storage architecture?
explanation: DASD stands for Direct Access Storage Device, referring to secondary storage where each record has a discrete address (like hard disks)[cite: 1].

question: Which disk geometry term describes the collection of tracks across all platters located at the exact same radial distance from the spindle?
explanation: A Cylinder is formed by the vertical stack of identical tracks across all magnetic platter surfaces in a multi-platter hard drive[cite: 5].

question: What is the smallest addressable physical unit of data storage on a traditional hard disk platter?
explanation: A Sector (typically 512 bytes on standard magnetic drives) is the smallest physical division of a track on a disk[cite: 5].

question: What is the primary function of the Switched Mode Power Supply (SMPS) inside a desktop computer?
options: Converting incoming high-voltage AC mains power into regulated, low-voltage DC power for internal components
explanation: An SMPS efficiently converts incoming AC power into various low-voltage DC levels (+3.3V, +5V, +12V) required by motherboard components[cite: 1, 5].

question: What color is standard on a desktop PC motherboard backplate to designate the 3.5mm analog Microphone Input port?
explanation: Under the PC 99 audio color coding standard, Pink represents the microphone input, Light Green is for line-out/headphones, and Light Blue is for line-in[cite: 5].

question: What color is standard on a computer audio port for connecting stereo headphones / front speakers?
explanation: Light Green is the standardized color for analog audio line-out/stereo headphone jacks on personal computers[cite: 5].

question: Which internal motherboard bridge controller directly handles communication between the CPU, RAM, and high-speed PCIe graphics cards?
explanation: The Northbridge (Memory Controller Hub) historically manages high-speed communication between the CPU, system RAM, and primary PCIe graphics buses[cite: 5].

question: What is the primary role of the Southbridge chipset component on a computer motherboard?
options: Managing lower-speed peripheral I/O interfaces like USB, SATA, BIOS ROM, and audio
Supplying high-voltage AC electrical power to fans
explanation: The Southbridge (I/O Controller Hub) manages slower expansion buses and peripheral interfaces including USB, audio, SATA, and legacy PCI[cite: 5].

question: What input device converts physical hand-drawn strokes into digital vector signals on a digitized drawing tablet?
explanation: A Stylus or digitizing pen is used with graphics tablets and touchscreens to input precise digital drawings and gestures[cite: 5].

question: What type of optical input technology scans human-made pencil or pen marks on pre-printed survey and examination sheets?
explanation: OMR (Optical Mark Recognition) detects marked shaded regions on questionnaires and objective examination answer sheets[cite: 5].

question: In a 9-digit bank MICR code found on cheque leaves, what do the first 3 digits represent?
explanation: The 9-digit MICR code structure consists of: First 3 digits = City Code, Middle 3 digits = Bank Code, Last 3 digits = Branch Code[cite: 5].

question: In a 9-digit bank MICR code, what do the middle 3 digits specify?
explanation: The middle three digits of a MICR code uniquely identify the specific Bank[cite: 5].

question: In a 9-digit bank MICR code, what do the final 3 digits indicate?
explanation: The last three digits of the MICR code pinpoint the individual Branch location of the bank[cite: 5].

question: What type of two-dimensional (2D) matrix barcode was invented in 1994 by the Japanese company Denso Wave?
explanation: Denso Wave, a subsidiary of Toyota, invented the Quick Response (QR) Code in 1994 for tracking automotive parts[cite: 5].

question: Which touchscreen technology uses an outer flexible layer pressed against a conductive glass substrate and is widely used in ATMs and POS kiosks?
explanation: Resistive touchscreens rely on physical pressure connecting two flexible conductive layers, making them durable for stylus and gloved use in ATMs[cite: 5].

question: Which touchscreen technology measures changes in electrostatic capacitance caused by the conductive touch of a human finger (used in smartphones)?
explanation: Capacitive touchscreens use the electrical conductivity of human skin to distort an electrostatic field, enabling responsive multi-touch in smartphones[cite: 5].

question: What is the process called when print jobs are sent to a temporary hard disk buffer so the CPU can continue processing other tasks?
explanation: Spooling (Simultaneous Peripheral Operations On-Line) intercepts print documents and manages them in a print queue on disk to free up application resources[cite: 5].

question: What is the term for restarting a computer that is already running by using warm-boot keystrokes without turning off main power?
explanation: Warm Booting (or soft rebooting) restarts the operating system while power remains applied to the motherboard[cite: 5].

question: What is starting up a computer from a completely powered-off state called?
explanation: Cold Booting occurs when electrical power is switched on to a cold machine, prompting full POST hardware checks and OS loading[cite: 5].

question: What term describes a discontinued hardware or software system that remains in service because it performs essential legacy functions?
explanation: A Legacy System is an outdated computer system or application that continues to be used because it satisfies core business needs[cite: 5].

question: What was the name of the first operational electronic computer developed in the US during WWII that utilized 18,000 vacuum tubes?
explanation: ENIAC contained approximately 18,000 vacuum tubes and became operational in late 1945[cite: 1, 5].

question: Which of the following early computers was built by the U.S. National Bureau of Standards (NBS) in 1950?
explanation: SEAC (Standards Eastern Automatic Computer) was a first-generation electronic computer built in 1950 by the US National Bureau of Standards[cite: 1].

question: Who created the first commercial portable laptop computer, the Osborne 1, in 1981?
explanation: Adam Osborne released the Osborne 1 in 1981, widely considered the first commercially successful portable microcomputer[cite: 5].

question: Who invented the optical compact disc (CD) in the late 1960s?
explanation: James Russell is credited with inventing the optical recording technology that formed the foundation for Compact Discs (CDs)[cite: 5].

question: Who led the IBM team that invented the 8-inch flexible magnetic floppy disk in 1971?
explanation: Alan Shugart at IBM developed the first commercial floppy disk drive in 1971[cite: 5].

question: What 19th-century mechanical calculating machine built by Charles Babbage in 1822 was designed to compute polynomial tables?
explanation: Charles Babbage designed the Difference Engine in 1822 to automatically calculate and tabulate polynomial mathematical functions[cite: 5].

question: What general-purpose mechanical computer designed by Charles Babbage in 1834 included a store (memory) and a mill (CPU)?
explanation: The Analytical Engine (1834) incorporated programmable logic, punch card input, working memory (the Store), and a processing core (the Mill)[cite: 1, 5].

question: What ancient calculating tool consisting of a wooden frame with sliding beads on parallel rods is considered the earliest counting machine?
explanation: The Abacus, developed in ancient civilizations, is one of the earliest mechanical calculating aids consisting of beads moved on rods[cite: 1, 5].

question: What term describes the demographic and economic disparity between individuals with regular access to computers and the Internet and those without?
explanation: The Digital Divide refers to the socioeconomic gap between populations that have access to modern information technologies and those that do not[cite: 5].

question: What is an extra single bit appended to binary data streams to detect errors during data transmission called?
explanation: A Parity Bit is an error-checking bit appended to a binary block to ensure the total number of 1-bits is even or odd[cite: 5].

question: What was the first microcomputer/personal computer kit built with the Intel 8080 CPU, released in 1975?
explanation: The MITS Altair 8800, introduced in 1975, was the microcomputer that sparked the personal computer revolution[cite: 5].

question: What was the name of the research organization Palo Alto Research Center (PARC) that developed Ethernet, the GUI, and laser printing?
explanation: Xerox PARC (Palo Alto Research Center) pioneered graphical user interfaces, bitmapped displays, Ethernet networking, and the computer mouse[cite: 5].

question: Which impact printer incorporates a metal or plastic wheel with embossed characters on radial spokes, similar to a typewriter?
explanation: A Daisy Wheel printer is an impact printer that uses a rotating disc with embossed characters to strike an inked ribbon against paper[cite: 5].

question: Can a Daisy Wheel printer produce graphic illustrations or vector charts?
options: No, it can only print pre-formed text characters on its petals
explanation: Daisy Wheel printers cannot print graphics because they rely strictly on molded typewriter-style character heads[cite: 5].

question: What is the speed measurement metric used for impact Dot Matrix and Daisy Wheel character printers?
explanation: Character printers print one symbol at a time and are rated in CPS (Characters Per Second)[cite: 5].

question: What high-speed line impact printer metric is used to measure printing output rate?
explanation: Line printers (such as drum or chain printers) print an entire line at once and are rated in LPM (Lines Per Minute)[cite: 5].

question: What is the total number of Primary Partitions supported on a single Master Boot Record (MBR) hard disk drive?
explanation: The legacy MBR partitioning scheme allocates partition table space for up to 4 primary partitions[cite: 5].

question: Which drive letters were historically reserved for floppy disk drives in MS-DOS and Microsoft Windows?
explanation: Drive letters A: and B: were historically reserved for primary and secondary floppy disk drives, with C: assigned to the main hard drive[cite: 5].

question: What is the total number of individual bits in a standard single-precision float or integer register on a 32-bit CPU?
explanation: A 32-bit microprocessor register contains 32 individual binary bits (equal to 4 bytes)[cite: 5].

question: What is an optical character reading device designed to convert printed or handwritten text images into editable digital text files?
explanation: OCR (Optical Character Recognition) software inspects scanned images of text documents and translates them into machine-editable text files[cite: 5].

question: What hardware device designed to assist visually impaired individuals translates screen text into raised mechanical Braille characters?
explanation: A Refreshable Braille Display is an electro-mechanical terminal that raises dynamic pin patterns to allow blind users to read text[cite: 5].

question: What is a 3D printing manufacturing technique that builds three-dimensional objects layer by layer using melted thermoplastic filament?
explanation: Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) is an additive manufacturing process that extrudes heated thermoplastic filaments layer upon layer[cite: 5].

question: What type of connector cable has an identical, reversible oval plug on both ends for data, video, and charging?
explanation: USB Type-C features a reversible, symmetric 24-pin connector design that fits into ports in either orientation[cite: 5].

question: What is the process of re-encoding and packaging data before transmitting it across a different network protocol layer called?
explanation: Encapsulation wraps data with protocol headers and trailers at each layer of the network stack before transmission[cite: 1].

question: What network hardware device connects two or more networks running different protocols and serves as their entry/exit gateway?
explanation: A Gateway translates communication between networks utilizing different architectures, protocols, and data formatting structures[cite: 1].

question: What type of malicious code remains dormant inside an operating system or software until specific logic conditions or dates are met?
explanation: A Logic Bomb is malicious code intentionally inserted into a software system that executes when predetermined conditions or dates occur[cite: 1, 5].

question: What type of hacker conducts security vulnerability assessments with legal authorization to help organizations remediate flaws?
explanation: White Hat (ethical) hackers use their cybersecurity skills with explicit authorization to identify and fix security vulnerabilities[cite: 1, 5].

question: What term describes a cybercriminal who breaks into computer networks with malicious or illegal intent?
explanation: A Cracker (or Black Hat hacker) breaks into systems without authorization for illegal personal gain, theft, or sabotage[cite: 1, 5].

question: What type of malware restricts access to user files by encrypting them and demands payment for the decryption key?
explanation: Ransomware holds victim data hostage through strong cryptographic encryption until a ransom is paid[cite: 1, 5].

question: What dedicated file storage hardware provides local area network (LAN) client devices with centralized disk storage over Ethernet?
explanation: Network Attached Storage (NAS) is a dedicated file-level data storage device connected directly to an Ethernet network[cite: 1].

question: In decimal to hexadecimal radix conversion, what mathematical operation is repeatedly executed on the quotient?
explanation: Converting a decimal integer to hexadecimal requires successive division by 16 while noting the remainder at each step[cite: 1].

question: In decimal to hexadecimal conversion, how are the recorded remainders read to form the final hexadecimal number?
options: Top to bottom (first remainder is MSD)
Bottom to top in reverse order (last remainder is MSD)
explanation: The remainders from successive divisions are transcribed in reverse order (from bottom to top), where the final remainder is the Most Significant Digit[cite: 1].

question: What base (radix) is utilized by the Hexadecimal numeral system?
explanation: The Hexadecimal system uses Base 16, comprising 16 alphanumeric symbols: digits 0–9 and letters A–F[cite: 1].

question: In hexadecimal numbering, what numerical decimal value is represented by the letter 'D'?
explanation: In hexadecimal: A=10, B=11, C=12, D=13, E=14, and F=15[cite: 5].

question: What layer of the OSI reference model is often referred to as the 'Heart of the OSI Model'?
explanation: Layer 4 (Transport Layer) acts as the bridge connecting the lower hardware layers to the upper software layers, earning the title 'Heart of the OSI model'[cite: 1].

question: Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for framing, physical MAC addressing, and node-to-node error control?
explanation: The Data Link Layer (Layer 2) divides packets into physical frames and manages MAC addresses, access control, and error detection[cite: 1].

question: What are the lower three layers of the OSI model (Physical, Data Link, and Network) collectively referred to as?
explanation: Layers 1, 2, and 3 are known as the Hardware or Lower Media Layers, while Layers 5, 6, and 7 are Software/Host layers[cite: 1].

question: What is the peak computational processing capacity of the PARAM Yuva II supercomputer developed by C-DAC in 2013?
explanation: PARAM Yuva II, unveiled in 2013 by C-DAC, achieved a peak performance capacity of 529 Teraflops[cite: 1].

question: What does the abbreviation HTML stand for in web publishing?
explanation: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language, the standard document formatting language of the Web[cite: 1, 5].

question: What utility program in Microsoft Windows reorganizes fragmented files on a magnetic disk to contiguous storage locations?
explanation: Disk Defragmenter consolidates fragmented file clusters on a hard drive to speed up file read and access times[cite: 1, 5].

question: What is Microsoft 365 sold as compared to traditional perpetual retail Microsoft Office bundles?
explanation: Microsoft 365 is a recurring subscription service that provides ongoing cloud updates and storage alongside desktop apps[cite: 1].

question: What is the digital notetaking and multi-user idea-sharing application included in the Microsoft Office suite?
explanation: Microsoft OneNote is a digital notebook application for capturing, organizing, and sharing notes, screen clippings, and sketches[cite: 1].

question: What is the relational database management system (RDBMS) program included in professional editions of Microsoft Office?
explanation: Microsoft Access is an entry-level relational database management software tool combining a database engine with a graphical UI[cite: 1, 5].

question: What is the desktop publishing application in Microsoft Office tailored for creating business cards, flyers, and brochures?
explanation: Microsoft Publisher is an office application designed for page layout and marketing publication designs[cite: 1].

question: What mobile digital cellular access technology uses spread-spectrum techniques and orthogonal codes?
explanation: CDMA (Code Division Multiple Access) is a digital wireless standard where multiple transmitters share the same frequency band using unique spread-spectrum codes[cite: 1].

question: What is a 100 Mbps optical fiber local area network standard based on dual-token ring architecture called?
explanation: FDDI (Fiber Distributed Data Interface) is an optical token ring standard providing 100 Mbps data transmission over fiber-optic lines[cite: 1].

question: What is an interface called that allows users to issue text commands directly to the operating system via a command prompt?
explanation: A CLI (Command Line Interface) requires users to type text commands to interact with system utilities and processes[cite: 1].

question: In public-key asymmetric cryptography, which key is used by a recipient to verify a sender's digital signature?
explanation: A digital signature is created using the sender's private key and verified by anyone using the sender's corresponding public key[cite: 1].

question: Which Microsoft Excel chart type is ideal for displaying categorical proportional percentages that sum to 100%?
explanation: A Pie Chart illustrates proportion and percentage contributions of individual categories to a whole[cite: 1].

question: Which professional social networking platform focuses on business networking, job recruiting, and corporate profiles?
explanation: LinkedIn is a web and mobile service designed specifically for professional networking and career development[cite: 1, 5].

question: Which XML-based default word processing file format was introduced starting with Microsoft Word 2007?
explanation: .docx is the default OpenXML compressed document format introduced in Office 2007 to reduce file size and enhance stability[cite: 1, 5].

question: In Microsoft Word, what custom dictionary feature allows technical terms or acronyms to be excluded from grammar/spell checking?
explanation: An Exclusion Dictionary specifies words that standard spelling check routines should flag or ignore based on customized organizational rules[cite: 1].

question: What is the web portal launched by the Indian Department of Telecommunications for citizens to view mobile tower radiation (EMF) compliance?
explanation: Tarang Sanchar is the Indian DoT portal that allows the public to view mobile tower locations and EMF emission compliance status[cite: 1].

question: What is a plain text file format where individual data field values within a record are separated by commas?
explanation: A CSV (Comma Separated Values) file stores tabular data as plain text, using commas to delimit individual data columns[cite: 1].

question: Which top-level domain (TLD) extension is reserved exclusively for accredited educational institutions?
explanation: The .edu TLD is restricted to accredited colleges, universities, and educational institutions[cite: 1].

question: Which top-level domain (TLD) extension is designated exclusively for official government entities and departments?
explanation: The .gov TLD is reserved for official governmental agencies and departments[cite: 1].

question: What does the abbreviation GPRS stand for in mobile cellular data communications?
explanation: GPRS (General Packet Radio Service) is a packet-oriented mobile data standard used in 2G and 3G cellular systems[cite: 1].

question: What does the abbreviation MPEG stand for in digital video and audio compression standards?
explanation: MPEG stands for Moving Picture Experts Group, the working group that develops international media compression standards[cite: 1].

question: What does the acronym VR represent in computer graphics and simulated environments?
explanation: Virtual Reality (VR) uses computer modeling to immerse users in a simulated 3D interactive environment[cite: 1].

question: What does the network acronym FQDN stand for in internet host addressing?
explanation: FQDN (Fully Qualified Domain Name) is the complete domain name specifying the exact host and hierarchy location in the DNS tree[cite: 1].

question: What does the acronym BIOS stand for in computer hardware architecture?
explanation: BIOS stands for Basic Input Output System, the firmware executed during boot-up to initialize hardware[cite: 1, 5].

question: Which of the following early computers was built using vacuum tubes and belongs to the First Generation of computers?
explanation: EDVAC (Electronic Discrete Variable Automatic Computer) was a first-generation vacuum-tube computer[cite: 1, 5].

question: What does the computer acronym ULSI stand for in microchip manufacturing?
explanation: ULSI stands for Ultra Large Scale Integration, packing millions of transistors onto a single microchip[cite: 1, 5].

question: What functional key is used in Microsoft Windows to enter edit mode for renaming a selected file or folder?
explanation: F2 activates the in-place text renaming box for any selected file or folder in Windows[cite: 1, 3].

question: What is the core computer software program that manages all system hardware resources, memory, and running applications?
explanation: An Operating System (OS) is the primary system software that controls computer hardware and allocates resources to applications[cite: 1, 5].

question: What is the state called when an operating system or software stops responding to keyboard and mouse inputs?
explanation: A System Hang (or Freeze) occurs when an application or the OS encounters an unresponsive state and halts processing[cite: 1].

question: What is the single-user, single-tasking command-line operating system developed by Microsoft in 1981 called?
explanation: MS-DOS (Microsoft Disk Operating System) is a non-graphical, single-tasking, single-user command-line operating system[cite: 1, 5].

question: What is the small high-speed memory placed between the CPU core and main memory to accelerate data retrieval called?
explanation: Cache Memory is a high-speed SRAM buffer located between the CPU and RAM to store frequently accessed data[cite: 1, 5].

question: What two core parts make up a machine-level computer instruction?
explanation: A machine instruction consists of an Opcode (operation code specifying the task) and an Operand (specifying data or registers)[cite: 1].

question: What component of the Central Processing Unit carries out all basic arithmetic addition, subtraction, and logical comparisons?
explanation: The ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) executes all mathematical calculations and boolean logical operations[cite: 1, 5].

question: What type of computer memory loses its stored data immediately when electrical power is switched off?
explanation: Volatile memory (such as dynamic RAM and static RAM) requires continuous electrical current to maintain its stored information[cite: 1, 5].
